curriculum.subject: Mathematics
curriculum.keyInquiryQuestion: How can we align a 2-digit number and a 1-digit number vertically in order to add? When do we regroup?
curriculum.suggestedLearningExperience: Learners in pairs to write addition sentences given in horizontal form vertically according to place value. Learners to add a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number without and with regrouping. Learners to practice addition by skipping on the number line. Learners in pairs/groups to collect different safe objects and use them in addition of 3-single digit numbers. Learners in pairs/groups to practice breaking numbers apart to make a 10. Learners in pairs to come up with different ways of adding two 2-digit numbers without and with regrouping. Learners to play digital games involving addition. Learners in groups to make patterns using numbers up to 100.
pertinentAndContemporaryIssues: ESD: DRR; safety - as learners collect objects; Citizenship: social cohesion - when working in groups

studentJourneyDraft.title: Welcome!
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: Today we learn addition! Adding means putting groups together to find the total.

studentJourneyDraft.title: Our Mission
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: work out missing numbers in patterns involving addition of whole numbers up to 100

studentJourneyDraft.title: Think First!
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: If you have 2 bananas and mama gives you 8 more, how many bananas do you have altogether?

interaction.prompt: If you have 2 bananas and mama gives you 8 more, how many bananas do you have altogether?
interaction.hint: Start at 2 and count forward 8 more!

studentJourneyDraft.title: Learn It
studentJourneyDraft.studentText:
Addition uses the + sign. We add two numbers to get a sum (the total).

**Example:** 2 + 8 = ?

Start at 2. Count forward 8.

**2 + 8 = 10**

**Tip:** Always start with the bigger number and count forward!

studentJourneyDraft.title: Real Life Connection
studentJourneyDraft.studentText:
You use addition every day:
• Counting all your books together
• Adding prices at the market
• Finding how many people are in a group
• Counting your savings!
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: When do you see this in your daily life? Think about your home, school, and market!

interaction.prompt: Where do you see this in real life? Give an example.

studentJourneyDraft.title: Watch and Learn
studentJourneyDraft.studentText:
**Worked Example:** 25 + 17 = ?

Step 1: Add the ones: 5 + 7 = 12. Write 2, carry 1.
Step 2: Add the tens: 2 + 1 + 1 (carried) = 4.

Answer: **25 + 17 = 42**

You can also count on: start at 25, count forward 17!

studentJourneyDraft.title: Your Turn!
studentJourneyDraft.studentText:
**Solve these:**
1) 14 + 9 = ?
2) 23 + 18 = ?
3) 35 + 27 = ?
4) A shop has 28 oranges and 15 mangoes. How many fruits altogether?

*Show your working!*
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: Start with the bigger number. Count forward. For harder ones, add ones first then tens.

interaction.hint: Start with the bigger number. Count forward. For harder ones, add ones first then tens.

studentJourneyDraft.title: Think About Your Learning
studentJourneyDraft.owlText: How do you add two numbers together? What helps you get the right answer?
